payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Change the background into a basketball court
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is there visible evidence that the background has begun changing toward a basketball court, even though the requested court background is not complete?
node.criteria: Pass if the image shows a discernible but incomplete change of the background toward a basketball court. Fail if there is no visible progress toward that change. Unknown if progress cannot be distinguished from the original or assessed reliably.
node.binding: Assess progress only toward replacing the background with a basketball court; unrelated edits do not count.

node_traces.evidence: The kitchen background has been replaced with a dark basketball-court-like setting, including a hoop, basketballs, and court markings. This is clear progress toward the requested court background, though the court is not fully complete.

fulfillment: The node’s binding is too vague and its completion criterion is inconsistent with the traces: s1 describes a court with visible markings and equipment, while s2 explicitly says the court is not fully complete, yet both pass and the node returns complete. Clarify that completion requires the background itself to read as a basketball court, using visible court features as evidence; treat “court-like” or partial features as progress, not completion. Preserve the existing partial/no/unknown distinctions and do not let equipment alone establish completion. The edited image visibly has a hoop, basketballs, and court markings, so the reference yes is supported here; the issue is robustness of the criterion, not negative visual evidence. No transport or schema failure is indicated.

response.content: {"text":"The trace supports the reference yes: the kitchen has been replaced by a recognizable basketball-court setting, with a hoop, court lines, and basketballs. The problem is criterion consistency, not missing visual progress: this node asks only whether the background has begun changing, so it can pass on partial court-like evidence even when the requested background is not complete. Clarify the distinction between progress and completion across the decision path: partial court features should support progress, while completion requires the background itself to read as a basketball court; equipment alone is insufficient. Preserve fail for no visible requested progress and unknown when evidence is unreliable. Keep the binding specific to the background replacement, and do not treat low confidence or repeated variation as proof that the edit is absent. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated."}
